key_insight: PIML-OFEM combines overlapping finite elements with problem-independent machine learning to reuse local basis functions across loads and boundary conditions for large-scale heterogeneous structures.
engineering_relevance: It enables faster high-resolution structural analysis and topology optimization while maintaining accuracy close to fine-scale finite element results.
method: Keep only corner-node degrees of freedom in each substructure.
Build oversampled basis functions on extended domains, then restrict them to the target region.
Use a U-Net to predict local basis functions from Young's modulus maps and blend them with partition of unity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with fine-scale finite element displacement and elemental strain energy, lower online cost than direct FEM, and improved accuracy over linear-interpolation PIML substructure models.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and generalization of the learned basis prediction across heterogeneous material distributions and problem settings.
paper_title: PIML-OFEM: A New Large-Scale Structural Analysis Method Based on Problem-Independent Machine Learning and Overlapping Finite Element Technique
